shouldFix.title: The Ed25519 record and signed preimage still lack one canonical encoding at every byte/string boundary
evidence: The preimage calls memberSha256 and payloadDigest merely 64-hex. result.payloadDigest and builderRootDigest likewise say 64-hex. The same contract explicitly says 64-hex lowercase for peCoffImageDigest, measuredBootTranscriptDigest, package-db digests, and builderPublicKey, so there is no global lowercase convention that closes the omitted cases.

For one 32-byte digest, both lowercase 000102...1f and uppercase 000102...1F satisfy ordinary 64-hex syntax but yield different canonical compact JSON bytes. A concrete reconstruction produced SHA-256(preimage) 7247bbcdf4783e2fb590e0aeb0f3cf3257466b7a2bc699498e0da93894b77645 for lowercase and 9c7057c21098b0c052c22d4c4872a6253a02415d36300924ecc73faf3d02f3c0 when memberSha256 and payloadDigest used uppercase. Both preserve the same underlying digest bytes.

The exact signed/later record gives builderPublicKey a 64-hex-lowercase wire encoding, but builderSignature is only described as a 64-byte value or opaque bytes. No carrier encoding or strict decode rule says whether the signed field is native bytes, 128-hex, base64, or another representation.

Concrete divergence: a builder serializes an uppercase member digest and a 128-hex signature. One verifier preserves the admitted spelling and decodes hex; another lower-normalizes the digest and expects a native byte string. The first verifies while the second reconstructs another message or rejects the record. Nothing in v42 selects one behavior.
shouldFix.impact: The structural kexec-absent proof is semantically complete but not byte-reproducible across conforming carrier and verifier implementations. A valid Linux entry can verify or refuse solely because of unstated digest case and signature-field encoding choices.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Pin every digest string used in builderAttestation.preimage and every builderRootDigest occurrence to one encoding, preferably exactly 64 lowercase hex with non-canonical spellings refused. Pin builderSignature's signed/later carrier encoding and strict decoding to exactly 64 signature bytes, and state that verify consumes those decoded bytes. Add uppercase/mixed-case digest, malformed signature encoding, wrong decoded length, and canonical round-trip vectors.

shouldFix.title: The reserved G22 vectors do not cover all refusal branches introduced by the governing marker and header-kind repairs
evidence: The governing marker grammar now covers zero/zero, lone start, lone end, reversed markers, extra starts, extra ends, nested, and overlapping occurrences. The required G22 string names only lone IKCFG_ST, reversed markers, and one valid pair plus stray ED. It omits lone IKCFG_ED, a valid pair plus stray ST, multi-start/multi-end, nested, and overlapping vectors.

There are six ordered cross-kind mismatches among x86-setup-0x1f1, arm64-zimg-loaded, and arm64-image-0x38. The required vector roster names only x86 signed with arm64-image-0x38. It does not name x86 to arm64-zimg, either arm64 branch to x86, or the two arm64 cross-branch mismatches.

The field is the contract's RESERVED-as-G22-evidence required-vector roster. A future harness can satisfy every listed item without executing several branches whose deterministic refusal was the substance of PTCB-V41-S1/S2.
This is test-closure rather than a surviving semantic ambiguity: v42's marker cardinality and actualHeaderKind equality themselves are explicit.
shouldFix.impact: G22 can later report the named design exercised while parser and dispatch bugs in unlisted refusal branches remain undetected. The successor does not fully carry the predecessor's requested malformed-class and every-cross-kind vector coverage.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Enumerate vectors for zero/zero acceptance, lone ST, lone ED, every extra-marker cardinality and side, reversed, nested, overlapping, all three correct header mappings, and all six ordered cross-kind mismatches. Also name signed/later builderPublicKey mismatch and root/key/signature cross-event composition vectors for the new retained-key join.
